title: Make ingest faster
prompt:
Objective: make Spawn's event ingest faster without changing what it ingests.

The metric is the sum, over six typical payloads (three Claude Code hook payloads and three Codex JSON lines), of the mean nanoseconds per call of `spawn_core::ingest::claude_hook` and `spawn_core::ingest::codex_line`. Lower is better.

How you are judged (rsi/scenarios/002.sh with the controller's bench rsi/scenarios/assets/ingest_objective.rs; read both, but do not edit them):
1. Behaviour must not change: on a randomized corpus of about 260 payloads (every hook and item type, malformed JSON, missing fields, unicode, long error text), your tree must produce byte-identical serialized events, source_event_ids, `None` results and errors as the baseline.
2. Your median over interleaved runs must be at least 5% below the baseline's median.
3. Every other scenario in rsi/scenarios must still pass.

Constraints:
- Keep the public signatures `claude_hook(&str) -> Result<Option<Normalized>, IngestError>` and `codex_line(&str) -> Result<Option<Normalized>, IngestError>`, and the fields of `Normalized`. The bench calls them.
- Do not change `EventKind` variants or their serde representation: the event log and every reader depend on them.
- Payloads are generated at random each run, so caching or special-casing inputs does not help.
- Only `crates/spawn-core/src` is measured: the bench is built with the baseline's manifests, so dependency or Cargo.toml changes are not honored, and any build.rs or .cargo/ change is rejected.

Measure locally with `cargo run --release -p spawn-core --example ingest_bench` (same payload shapes). Make one focused improvement per task, keep `cargo test -p spawn-core` passing, and stop when your change is measurably faster.
